nodes.rationale: The voice alone leaves a woman a man in game, so a woman has Female among Configuration.Flags beside the woman's voice.

nodes.label: SKILL.md format (name + description frontmatter)
nodes.rationale: The description is the text an agent selects a skill on, so it must say when to use the skill, not only what it is.

nodes.label: Examples kept unlike the eval's authoring tasks
nodes.norm_label: examples kept unlike the eval's authoring tasks
nodes.rationale: The example records use another element or kind than the tasks of scripts/eval-ollama.mjs, so the eval measures a model working its record out of the tables rather than copying an example.

nodes.label: Skill discovery (cached per process)
nodes.rationale: Discovery walks each collection for SKILL.md files, so adding or editing a skill needs no rebuild; but discoverSkills() caches the result per process, so a running server keeps the old set until restarted.

nodes.label: Change an example only after building it on a test instance
nodes.norm_label: change an example only after building it on a test instance
nodes.rationale: Examples and table rows are copied by models as written, so each must be proven to build before it lands.

nodes.label: Vanilla record tables in each SKILL.md
nodes.norm_label: vanilla record tables in each skill.md
nodes.rationale: Models read SKILL.md and seldom REFERENCE.md, and every table value is a Skyrim.esm record, so the tables let a model write those values without a search.

nodes.label: ModManager seam (SKYRIM_MOD_MANAGER=mo2|amethyst)
nodes.rationale: Chosen by configuration and never inferred from the operating system; the tools are the same for every manager.

nodes.label: Platform seam (chosen once from the OS in createBackend())
nodes.norm_label: platform seam (chosen once from the os in createbackend())

nodes.label: Backend seam (Backend.ts, SkyrimBackend, AppBackend)
nodes.rationale: Constructing a backend never touches the network, and connect() is the credential check only, so an unreadable instance or unbuilt helper surfaces with its own cause on the first call.

nodes.label: ADR-0007: The operating system and the mod manager are separate seams
nodes.norm_label: adr-0007: the operating system and the mod manager are separate seams
nodes.rationale: OS and mod manager vary independently (MO2 runs on both systems). Rejected: one seam where Linux means Amethyst, tools per mod manager (twice the tools); a Docker image deferred.

nodes.label: CI OS matrix (ubuntu-24.04, windows-latest)
nodes.rationale: Every push and pull request runs on Windows and Linux (ADR-0007); Markdown changes run too, because the guides and skills are served at runtime and their tests read the real files.

nodes.label: Retry only what was refused before it ran, and only once
nodes.norm_label: retry only what was refused before it ran, and only once
nodes.rationale: isSessionExpired() is true only for errors that prove nothing was applied; a refused credential is latched and never retried, because password retries lock the account.

nodes.label: Amethyst deploy adds only what is new
nodes.norm_label: amethyst deploy adds only what is new
nodes.rationale: Amethyst cannot be told to re-read its files and overwrites outside changes to lines it knows, so deploy adds only new lines and runs Amethyst's deploy only when its window is closed.

nodes.label: Lower-cased path lookups on every system
nodes.norm_label: lower-cased path lookups on every system
nodes.rationale: Linux file systems are case-sensitive and Skyrim's files are not; comparing lower-cased paths everywhere lets the Windows test suite exercise it.

nodes.label: PermanentBackendError (refused credential latched)
nodes.rationale: For a password or client secret every retry is one more failed logon, and enough of those lock the account for everyone.

nodes.label: The Creation Kit's role (headless compiler, pull after GUI work)
nodes.norm_label: the creation kit's role (headless compiler, pull after gui work)
nodes.rationale: Records are edited in the project, not in the CK; work done in the CK window must be pulled back before the next deploy or the deploy refuses to overwrite it.

nodes.label: Links written as editor IDs (resolvedLinks, links.lock.json)
nodes.norm_label: links written as editor ids (resolvedlinks, links.lock.json)
nodes.rationale: links.lock.json keeps what each link to the load order named, so a mod installed later whose record has the same editor ID does not change it.

nodes.label: Header version 1.70 / 1.71
nodes.rationale: 1.71 widened the range of new record numbers; a 1.71 plugin on an older game likely crashes it, so write the header the target game expects.

nodes.label: Patch plugin
nodes.rationale: Patches resolve conflicts; editing either mod's plugin is undone by its next update.

nodes.label: Plugin header flags and masters list
nodes.norm_label: plugin header flags and masters list

nodes.label: Project layout (plugin, scripts, assets, build)
nodes.rationale: A deploy makes the mod folder exactly build/ plus assets/, so every file the mod needs belongs in the project or the next deploy removes it.

nodes.label: The rule of one (last override wins whole)
nodes.norm_label: the rule of one (last override wins whole)

nodes.label: Mod as a project (text in git, one file per record)
nodes.norm_label: mod as a project (text in git, one file per record)
nodes.rationale: An override written into your own project is a patch that survives the other mod's next update; an edit to its plugin does not.

nodes.label: An assigned FormID is permanent
nodes.rationale: Saves and other plugins point at a record's FormID, so renumbering it or deleting and re-creating it breaks every one of them.

nodes.norm_label: nexus mods api (v1 rest, v2 graphql, v3 rest)

nodes.label: A fitting file
nodes.rationale: A file fits only when it names this game version or a range holding it and was uploaded after that version came out, since a range written earlier cannot know it.

nodes.label: Install the fitting file over the mod (replace + exact name)
nodes.norm_label: install the fitting file over the mod (replace + exact name)
nodes.rationale: Without name set to the mod's name as checkGameVersion gives it, the file installs as a second mod beside the broken one.

nodes.label: Game-version fix workflow (keep save, check, fitting file, install, ask, recheck, report)
nodes.norm_label: game-version fix workflow (keep save, check, fitting file, install, ask, recheck, report)

nodes.label: Disable a mod only on the user's word
nodes.norm_label: disable a mod only on the user's word
nodes.rationale: A fitting file is the fix; disabling is the fallback, asked for each mod, because a mod disabled mid-playthrough can break the save and its missing masters can stop the game from starting.

nodes.rationale: The reference renders the tools as one product serves them, so each product generates and commits its own.

nodes.label: ToolError (errors say the next step)
nodes.rationale: A raw Error reaching a client becomes an opaque Internal error; a model reads the message and acts on it, so InvalidParams names what to send instead.

nodes.label: ADR-0009: The core is its own package, served by the MCP server and the OpenClaw plugin
nodes.norm_label: adr-0009: the core is its own package, served by the mcp server and the openclaw plugin
nodes.rationale: As an MCP server the project cannot control what OpenClaw does with it; an OpenClaw plugin can, so everything the tools do moves into a core package both products depend on. Rejected: plugin importing the MCP package, a workspace package inside the MCP repo, shipping the MCP server through the manifest's mcpServers.

nodes.label: Core-first rule
nodes.rationale: A change to a tool, an answer, a guide or a skill is made in the core, never only in a product; a product holds its transport and its client's glue, and the MCP server gets the nearest equivalent of what only one client can do.

nodes.label: Never write to stdout
nodes.rationale: The MCP server speaks MCP over stdio and runs the core in its process; anything on stdout that is not a protocol frame corrupts the stream and breaks every tool at once.

nodes.label: OpenClaw's limits on an MCP server (skyrim__ prefix, dropped instructions, extraDirs skills, Tool Search)
nodes.norm_label: openclaw's limits on an mcp server (skyrim__ prefix, dropped instructions, extradirs skills, tool search)

nodes.norm_label: project (a mod kept as text in git)

nodes.label: Care with a real backend
nodes.rationale: The tools write into a mod manager's instance; a Wabbajack-installed instance deletes every mod it did not install on its next update, so work on a test instance, change others' mods only through patches, and ask before deploying where you do not own.

nodes.label: Run write paths against a real backend once
nodes.norm_label: run write paths against a real backend once
nodes.rationale: A green suite does not mean a write path works: a fake accepts any order of calls and cannot know the backend's own rules, so what a real run teaches is encoded as an assertion.

nodes.norm_label: recordfiles.cs (record files checked before a build)

nodes.norm_label: recordlinks.cs (links written as editor ids made formids)

nodes.norm_label: deploy guards and clears the creation kit's copy in overwrite

nodes.label: Creation Kit command-line switches (-GenerateLips, -ConvertToESL)
nodes.rationale: Undocumented: each switch's argument syntax is verified against the Creation Kit before a tool relies on it.

nodes.label: Build keeps links as written; links.lock.json pins them
nodes.norm_label: build keeps links as written; links.lock.json pins them

nodes.label: buildProject corrections and warnings (corrected, built_with_warnings)
nodes.rationale: Mistakes with one plain fix (copied escapes, misplaced fields, copied FormKeys, taken editor IDs) are corrected rather than refused, because eval transcripts showed small models failing runs on such refusals.

nodes.label: FormKey rules (new record leaves FormKey out; build assigns it)
nodes.norm_label: formkey rules (new record leaves formkey out; build assigns it)

nodes.label: ADR-0004: A mod is authored as a text project, not as a plugin
nodes.norm_label: adr-0004: a mod is authored as a text project, not as a plugin
nodes.rationale: Claude edits the text with its ordinary file tools, so the server needs far fewer tools, and git gives diff, review and rollback for free.

nodes.label: ADR-0005: The Creation Kit is used only through its command line
nodes.norm_label: adr-0005: the creation kit is used only through its command line
nodes.rationale: The GUI loads slowly, interrupts with modal dialogs and its layout moves with every patch, so automation breaks silently; GUI automation and the CK as record editor were rejected.

nodes.label: Git referees deploy and pull
nodes.rationale: Deploy refuses to overwrite a plugin changed since the last deploy and pull refuses to write over uncommitted text; otherwise Creation Kit work would vanish on the next deploy.

nodes.label: Exact-text file edits refused (95 of gemma4:e4b's, rounds 40-47)
nodes.norm_label: exact-text file edits refused (95 of gemma4:e4b's, rounds 40-47)
nodes.rationale: 64 were the model's own (remembered values, wrong indentation, text never there); 31 were made stale by the build's corrections and editor-ID links written back as FormIDs.

nodes.norm_label: recipe stations, materials and smithing perks

nodes.label: Enchantments (cast type follows the item, worn restrictions)
nodes.norm_label: enchantments (cast type follows the item, worn restrictions)

nodes.label: Keywords carry the gameplay
nodes.rationale: Perks, merchants, crafting menus and the enchanting table look at keywords, not item type, so a new item without the right keywords is silently left out; copy the keyword set from the closest vanilla item.

nodes.label: Enchanted weapon build rules
nodes.rationale: A weapon enchantment is cast FireAndForget on Touch as its effects are, and a templated weapon carries its template's Data, keywords, Model and EquipmentType as every official one does; the build refuses either otherwise.

nodes.label: Tool annotations (readOnly, destructive, idempotent, openWorld hints)
nodes.norm_label: tool annotations (readonly, destructive, idempotent, openworld hints)
nodes.rationale: Hints, not a permission system: how a client decides what to auto-approve and what to put in front of a human.

nodes.label: Capability gate (fails open)
nodes.rationale: Every failure path leaves the gate empty and the list complete: hiding a tool that would have worked is worse than offering one that errors, because the first is invisible.

nodes.label: coerceArgs (argument sent as text taken as its declared type)
nodes.norm_label: coerceargs (argument sent as text taken as its declared type)

nodes.label: Compact single-level JSON envelope
nodes.rationale: Indentation costs response budget and buys a model nothing; wrapping twice nests JSON inside JSON.

nodes.label: Extending the server (tool, family, guide, skill, rename)
nodes.norm_label: extending the server (tool, family, guide, skill, rename)

nodes.label: A doc/code contradiction is a bug in one of them
nodes.norm_label: a doc/code contradiction is a bug in one of them

nodes.label: Every tool declares a title and all four annotation hints
nodes.norm_label: every tool declares a title and all four annotation hints
nodes.rationale: OpenAI's directory rejects a tool that omits a hint, and a client falling back to the defaults (not read-only, destructive, open-world) treats a new search tool like a delete.

nodes.label: tools/list is the truth about what you can call
nodes.norm_label: tools/list is the truth about what you can call

nodes.label: Router
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not generated, because the generated form can only restate the tools' own names back at the reader.

nodes.label: A status code is not a diagnosis (health())
nodes.norm_label: a status code is not a diagnosis (health())
nodes.rationale: An unreachable backend, a refused credential and a missing permission can arrive as the same HTTP status and need opposite fixes; a message naming a cause needs evidence for it.

nodes.label: Nexus gating exception (NEXUS_API_KEY, premium account)
nodes.rationale: The user's decision: Nexus tools are offered only with a key, and downloadNexusFile only when Nexus confirms a premium account; an unconfirmed key withholds the download.

nodes.label: Hand-written intent-to-tool map
nodes.rationale: Written by hand in the words people actually use, because a generated index can only ever say a tool's own name back.

nodes.label: Papyrus scripts and saves
nodes.rationale: A save stores every running script, its variables and events, so a scripted mod removed mid-playthrough leaves orphaned instances.

nodes.label: FaceGen files
nodes.rationale: The game loads pre-generated face files instead of building faces from the record, so any appearance change needs FaceGen regenerated in the Creation Kit.

nodes.label: The NPC record (NPC_ base, ACHR reference)
nodes.norm_label: the npc record (npc_ base, achr reference)

nodes.label: What a save keeps of an NPC
nodes.norm_label: what a save keeps of an npc

nodes.label: NPC templates and template flags
nodes.rationale: A field covered by a set template flag is ignored on the NPC itself, the most common cause of an edit with no effect on generic NPCs.

nodes.label: Saves, co-saves and testing on a copy
nodes.norm_label: saves, co-saves and testing on a copy
nodes.rationale: A disabled mod leaves orphaned traces and a mayNotWork DLL can corrupt a save silently, so the user keeps a copy of the latest save and tests on a copy.

nodes.label: Small local model with a 128k window as the design target
nodes.norm_label: small local model with a 128k window as the design target

nodes.label: Object value merged as a JSON merge patch
nodes.norm_label: object value merged as a json merge patch
nodes.rationale: e4b's first {BasicStats: {Damage: 12}} took the Iron Sword's value and weight with it when written whole (eval round 49).

nodes.label: Ollama gemma4 parser drops calls with a dotted key and a text value
nodes.norm_label: ollama gemma4 parser drops calls with a dotted key and a text value

nodes.label: set as a list of {path, value}
nodes.norm_label: set as a list of {path, value}

nodes.label: narrowingHint
nodes.rationale: Lives on the tool rather than in a table keyed by tool name, which goes stale silently on a rename.

nodes.label: Profiles core (12), readonly (9), all (17)
nodes.rationale: Every tool schema costs tokens and a client that cannot fetch schemas on demand pays for the whole list every turn; a profile is also a safety property, since readonly's write tools are not routed.

nodes.label: Response budget ceilings (core 24,000 B, readonly 32,000 B, all none)
nodes.norm_label: response budget ceilings (core 24,000 b, readonly 32,000 b, all none)
nodes.rationale: Over the ceiling the answer is replaced by valid JSON, never a cut-off fragment, which would not parse and which a model answers by retrying.

nodes.label: ADR-0001: The tool count is a cost, not a goal
nodes.norm_label: adr-0001: the tool count is a cost, not a goal
nodes.rationale: Measured: ~140 tools serialised to ~19,000 tokens per turn for a client without on-demand schema fetching, full coverage ~51,000; reliability on a small local model comes from better tools rather than more of them.

nodes.label: ADR-0002: Composite tools where the protocol is the hard part
nodes.norm_label: adr-0002: composite tools where the protocol is the hard part
nodes.rationale: Ordering and obligations (lock lifetime, unlock after a failure) cannot be typed into schemas; a rule a model must remember across four calls it will sometimes forget, and an orphaned lock blocks others.

nodes.label: ADR-0008: A record is also edited field by field, with no text to match
nodes.norm_label: adr-0008: a record is also edited field by field, with no text to match
nodes.rationale: For a small local model the exact-old-text file edit is the hard part; editRecord changes fields by path, refuses fields the type lacks and answers the new text so the next change starts from the file, not memory.

nodes.label: Demand is the evidence (coverage is a diagnostic, not a target)
nodes.norm_label: demand is the evidence (coverage is a diagnostic, not a target)

nodes.label: Composite tool with clean-up on every path
nodes.norm_label: composite tool with clean-up on every path
nodes.rationale: Leaves the backend no worse than it found it; a clean-up failure is reported, not thrown over the result; small profiles list the composite instead of the steps.

nodes.label: Distribution frameworks (runtime changes, no overrides)
nodes.rationale: They avoid record conflicts altogether by changing things at runtime from text files, so prefer them for broad additions.

nodes.label: Merged patches (Bashed Patch, Merged Patch, Synthesis)
nodes.norm_label: merged patches (bashed patch, merged patch, synthesis)

nodes.label: Wabbajack
nodes.rationale: Warn before changing a Wabbajack-installed instance: an update deletes unknown files and list authors usually void support for modified installs.

nodes.label: Leveled-list conflict fixes (merged patch, own sublist, SPID, script)
nodes.norm_label: leveled-list conflict fixes (merged patch, own sublist, spid, script)
nodes.rationale: Ranked best first: a merged patch keeps every mod's changes; one entry pointing at your own list keeps your content in a record nobody else touches; a runtime script lives in the save and cannot be undone by removing the mod.

nodes.label: Distribution instead of NPC edits (SPID)
nodes.rationale: Overrides conflict with every other mod touching those NPCs; SPID applies at runtime without overriding anything, so edit records only for specific NPCs.

nodes.label: The effect chain (shared MGEF records)
nodes.rationale: One MGEF is reused by many spells, potions and enchantments, so changing it changes all of them; make a copy for a new spell instead.

nodes.label: How perks reach magic (entry points, keywords)
nodes.norm_label: how perks reach magic (entry points, keywords)
nodes.rationale: Perks filter on an effect's keywords and school, so a new effect without the vanilla keywords gets none of the vanilla perks.

nodes.label: Spells (type, cast type, delivery, cost, half-cost perk)
nodes.norm_label: spells (type, cast type, delivery, cost, half-cost perk)

nodes.label: Magic workflow (new spell names a vanilla effect)
nodes.norm_label: magic workflow (new spell names a vanilla effect)
nodes.rationale: The effect is what a spell does, shared by every spell naming it; how strongly is the spell's own Data. A new MGEF is only for what no vanilla effect does, and a vanilla MGEF changes only when everything using it should change.

nodes.label: Spriggit (project text format, converter generated in the helper)
nodes.norm_label: spriggit (project text format, converter generated in the helper)

nodes.label: ADR-0003: Plugins are read and written by a Mutagen helper
nodes.norm_label: adr-0003: plugins are read and written by a mutagen helper
nodes.rationale: No maintained TypeScript library reads or writes Bethesda plugins; Mutagen already handles 1.70/1.71 headers, light plugins, localized strings and compressed records. Rejected: own TS reader/writer, the Spriggit CLI (needs .NET SDK and nuget.org), a TS reader plus Mutagen writer (two parsers that would disagree).

nodes.label: ADR-0006: The project is GPL-3.0, not MIT
nodes.norm_label: adr-0006: the project is gpl-3.0, not mit
nodes.rationale: Mutagen and most of the ecosystem (LOOT, Synthesis, Spriggit, houseCARL, Phostwood's crash-log rules) are GPL-3.0; keeping an MIT server at arm's length from a GPL helper over stdio would rest on a legally grey line, and GPL lets the project reuse that code.

nodes.label: Project plugin as Spriggit YAML text
nodes.norm_label: project plugin as spriggit yaml text

nodes.label: Leveled list workflow
nodes.rationale: An override replaces the whole list, so the copy keeps every entry of the winning version and every other mod's additions before yours are appended.

nodes.label: The server documents itself (MCP resources and tools)
nodes.norm_label: the server documents itself (mcp resources and tools)
nodes.rationale: Resources are usually user-attached, so an agent will not discover them on its own; a tool is already in its context. Both are drill-downs on purpose.

nodes.label: First-try success
nodes.rationale: The measure of quality: a task completed from a cold session without retrying, a wrong tool or asking for what the server could supply; tool count and token cost matter only through their effect on it.
